title: Cart Derby: On Your Own
subject: physical science
instructions: Answer on your own, even though you worked out carts with your group. Acceleration = net force ÷ mass. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.skill: I can find net force and acceleration
questions.prompt: Net Force: Fill in the net force and the acceleration for each cart.
questions.notes: Net force = push − friction; acceleration = net force ÷ mass. Look for 1.5 or 5 (the push divided by mass, friction forgotten) and 0.25 (10 ÷ 40, the push alone) in the last row.

questions.prompt: Steady Speed: A cart rolls at a steady 2 m/s on a flat floor. What is the net force on it?

options.text: Zero: the forces on it are balanced.
options.why: Yes: no net force means no change in speed.

options.text: 2 N forward, to keep it moving.
options.why: A moving object needs no net force to keep going.

options.text: The push must be bigger than the friction.
options.why: Then it would speed up, not stay steady.

options.text: It depends on the cart's mass.
options.why: Steady speed means balanced forces at any mass.

questions.skill: I can find net force and acceleration
questions.prompt: Double the Mass: The same net force pushes a cart with twice the mass. What happens to its acceleration?

options.why: More mass makes it harder to speed up.
Same force, more mass: less acceleration.
Yes: a = F ÷ m, and m doubled.
There's still a net force, so it speeds up.

questions.skill: I can find net force and acceleration
questions.prompt: Top Speed: A 50 kg cart starts from rest with a net force of 100 N. How fast is it going after 4 seconds?
questions.key: Acceleration = 100 ÷ 50 = 2 m/s²; speed = 2 × 4 = 8 m/s. Look for 2 (stopped at the acceleration) and 25 (100 ÷ 4).
